question.text: The pre-open session for equity derivatives on NSE primarily serves the purpose of:

answer.text: Facilitating order entry, modification, and cancellation before the regular market opens
Determining the opening price through a call auction
Allowing only institutional investors to place orders
Settling the previous day's outstanding positions

explanation.text: The Logic: In general industry practice, a pre-open session on the derivatives segment lets members stage their order book before continuous trading begins — entering new orders, modifying existing ones, and cancelling orders ahead of regular market open. It is an order-preparation window for the matching engine and is open to all members, not restricted to institutions. The Trap: The call-auction price-discovery mechanism is associated primarily with the equity cash pre-open, not the derivatives pre-open. Settlement of the previous day's positions is handled separately through clearing-and-settlement processes, not in a pre-open trading window. Note: The cited NISM-Series-VIII workbook pages (128-132) describe regular trading hours and order conditions but do not contain the specific pre-open session description (order entry, modification, and cancellation before regular open) used here. The framing above is general exchange-microstructure description rather than a direct workbook citation.
